title: Deep Principle Opens Free API for Hydrogen-1.0 Science AI Model
summary:
The Hangzhou startup has begun issuing access keys for its latest research tool, offering the service at no cost to users of compatible third-party clients or its own website. Deep Principle stated that the GPU and server costs for the Hydrogen-1.0 model are funded by the company's $HYDRO token, allowing the science-focused AI to be available via an OpenAI-compatible base URL.

The open-weight system is built on the GLM-5.3 model from Z.ai and was specialized using internal lab records and discovery trajectories. In performance tests, the model scored 38.3% on the FrontierScience-Research benchmark, surpassing the 33.3% posted by OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra, and recorded a 93% score on the PhD-level GPQA-Diamonds questionnaire.

selectedTweets.text:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: A Hangzhou startup says its open-weight AI model beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at scientific research.

• Hydrogen-1.0 is built on GLM-5.3, an open model from Chinese lab Z .ai
• Deep Principle trained it further on its own lab records, including how its scientists actually worked through problems
• FrontierScience-Research is a benchmark OpenAI built itself, with 60 multi-step research problems written by PhD scientists
• On it, Deep Principle reports 38.3% vs 33.3% for GPT-6 Astra
• It also reports 93% on GPQA Diamond, a set of PhD-level science questions written so the answers can't easily be looked up online
• The model is priced at the same rates as GLM-5.3 for anyone using it through an API

@sophiadew: "You actually wanna see all of the research notes, all the things that went wrong, everything that actually happened within the laboratory, and that's how you can train these models better for science."
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
We’re introducing Hydrogen-1.0, our first open-weight model for scientific research. We post-trained GLM-5.3 (@Zai_org) on our internal scientific data, lab records, and discovery trajectories.

It scores 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research vs GPT-6-Astra’s 33.3% and scores 93.0% on GPQA-Diamonds.

We believe science should be open, collaborative, and democratized, rather than proprietary. Only open weights let researchers inspect, adapt and build on the unprecedented speed of AI growth. There are many recent models named by chemical elements, but we believe Hydrogen-1.0 is the first aiming towards and open scientific superintelligence for discovery. 🧵
